query: Wire two DC motors and an HC-SR04 sensor to an Arduino Uno for a two-wheeled robot.
notes: KNOWN FAILING CASE as of 2026-08-14 — documents a real bug found while building this dataset, not a guess. tools/wiring_tools.py::allocate_pins keys its `assignments` dict by component_key ('dc_motor'), so requesting the same component twice (the single most common real scenario: a two-wheeled robot needs two motors) silently drops the first motor's pin assignment when the second overwrites it in the dict — even though `used` correctly reserved distinct pins for both under the hood. Live run on 2026-08-14 confirmed only one 'dc_motor' key survives in `assignments` with IN_A=12/IN_B=0 (pin 0 is also reserved — a second, separate issue). Expected behavior here is what SHOULD happen (two distinct motor entries); this case exists to catch the fix. Do not encode the current buggy single-entry output as 'expected'.
